parsed.explanation: The combined regime pairs a permissive state layer with a hostile federal layer. Positives: the 2016 birth-sex facility law was repealed (2017), no state facility ban or criminal offence exists, local ordinances cover ~30% of population, federal employment and hate-crime protections apply, courts are active. Exposives: federal visa screening orders refusal where sex is in doubt with possible lifetime fraud ineligibility (tier-2 state targeting of outed travellers); federal facility exclusion in government buildings; state custody funds no transition care; minors cannot obtain transition care; no state GI hate-crime coverage; no statewide accommodations protection. The violence figure is unusable (undercount, no denominator). Outing consequences are major-to-severe, not custodial-criminal, but the federal document/entry regime reaches every trans visitor.

entry_documents.exposure: Federal cable directs refusal where documents cast doubt on sex and consideration of permanent fraud ineligibility; 8+ foreign governments issued trans travel advisories over identity-document and data rules. Documented.
entry_documents.protection: Visa fraud finding requires all four elements, is never automatic, and has limited waivers; suit challenging passport policy is pending. Documented.
entry_documents.interaction: Entry refusal or document scrutiny escalates to lifetime ineligibility, which then follows the traveller across all states including this one.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: If detained: state funds barred for transition care (2025 law); federal corrections policy mandates hair-cutting, hormone removal, psychiatric substitution for trans inmates. Documented for custody settings.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: No state criminal offence for facility use here; no documented arrest practice in this state. Documented.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: A routine visitor encounter (bathroom complaint, ID check) could escalate to state custody where care is defunded; federal custody adds conversion policy.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Federal order bars trans people from federally funded single-sex facilities — applies in federal buildings here. State has no facility ban; 2025 bathroom bill revived but not enacted; 4 other states criminalize.
federal_state_facilities.protection: 2017 repeal means no state statute bars or criminalizes facility use matching gender identity; map shows this state among those without a ban.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Facility access depends on building owner: state/private permissive, federal exclusionary; the revived bill makes the state layer uncertain within a legislative term.

care_services.exposure: Trans minors barred from transition care (2023 laws, funds barred 2025); federal proposed rules would bar public-insurance reimbursement for under-18 care. Visiting minor and guardian face care denial. Documented.
care_services.protection: No documented restriction on adult visitors obtaining ordinary or transition-related care in this state; designated-visitor statute grants hospital visitation.
care_services.interaction: A family travelling with a trans minor moves from ordinary entry into a state where refill or emergency transition care can be refused, with no state-fund remedy.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Federal counterterrorism strategy targets 'radically pro-transgender' groups; justice department uses 'radical gender ideology' framing; advocates describe genocide-stage pattern. State layer shows no equivalent official hostility here.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Federal employment and national hate-crime statutes still cover gender identity; several federal orders blocked or enjoined.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Hostile federal framing reaches the visitor through national agencies and border officers, while state officials here are not documented as adopting it.

minors_guardians.exposure: State bans transition care under 18 and male-at-birth girls' sports; parents' rights law requires outing of name/pronoun requests in schools (affects any school visit). Federal order criminalises teachers facilitating social transition.
minors_guardians.protection: None documented for a visiting minor's care access in this state.
minors_guardians.interaction: A travelling family with a trans minor encounters care denial plus a mandated-disclosure school regime, though ordinary short visits rarely enter schools.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: State hate-crime statute covers neither gender identity nor sexual orientation, so bias assault may go uncharged; only 23 states cover GI. Killing figure (3.0/100k) is an acknowledged undercount with no denominator — unusable.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Federal hate-crime statute covers gender identity; federal employment discrimination bar applies; local ordinances cover ~30% of population.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Assault recourse depends on federal charging willingness in a climate where federal hostility is documented; state-level bias enhancement is unavailable.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No statewide public-accommodations, housing or private-employment protection; coverage is municipal and patchy (~30% of population). Passport and health-rule challenges unresolved.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Active litigation: ACLU suit, enjoined executive orders, courts striking exclusions; legal-aid FAQ maintains document guidance; 2022 court removed surgery requirement.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Remedies exist and function unevenly, but outcomes shift with which federal measures are in force at the moment of travel.

anchor_checks.comparison: Lower than this case: repeated trans-visitor detention in crowded cells, withheld care, delayed habeas, judges accepting police summaries, retaliation for complaints. Here no state criminalisation, no documented trans-visitor detention pattern, and courts actively hear challenges — custody harm exists only if detention occurs.

Similar in kind: entry-stage secondary screening, document divergence, refusal under discretion, humiliation and slow remedies. This dossier sits slightly below because a possible lifetime fraud ineligibility and multi-government travel advisories make the entry exposure more severe than administrative return-transport.

Higher than this case: equality law covering gender identity in public services with independent oversight producing apologies and compensation. Here state accommodation coverage is patchy, state hate-crime law omits gender identity, and federal policy affirmatively excludes — several compounding punitive provisions remain.

parsed.synthesis: The traveller encounters two regimes layered: a comparatively permissive state (facility ban repealed and not criminalised, local ordinances in the largest city, functioning courts) and a hostile federal government (document/entry screening with possible lifetime ineligibility, facility exclusion in federal buildings, conversion-oriented custody policy, hostile counterterrorism framing, care restrictions for minors). The federal layer is what every trans visitor passes through, so state tolerance cannot cancel it. Severity if outed is major (visa refusal, service denial, uncharged bias assault, care denial for a minor) rather than custodial-criminal, and litigation plus federal statutory protections provide real but uneven recourse. Absence of documented street violence is unproven, not safety; the killing figure is unusable without a denominator.
